outputs.exact_statement: For every prime $p$, finite $p$-group $G$, subgroup $H\le G$, and integer $n\ge0$, $$\boxed{r_n(G,H)=\ell(G,H).}$$
For every finite $p$-group $G$, subgroup $H$, and $n\ge0$, $r_n(G,H)\le\ell(G,H)$.

Let $\mathcal C_m^G$ be the category of genuine $G$-spectra localized by the inflated sphere $L_m^fS$. It is rigidly compactly generated. Its compact tensor-triangular spectrum is the finite subspace $$\{(H,i):H\le G\text{ up to conjugacy},\ 0\le i\le m\}$$ of the equivariant spectrum, with $(H,i)$ representing $\mathcal P_i^G(H)$. The image of a finite genuine spectrum is compact and dualizable. An object $Z\in\mathcal C_m^G$ is zero if and only if $$T(i)\wedge\Phi^H Z=0
 \qquad(H\le G,\ 0\le i\le m).$$ For the image of a finite object, its support is tested equally by $T(i)$ and $K(i)$ at these heights. For every compact object of $\mathcal C_m^G$, membership in the support at $(H,i)$ is equivalent to nonvanishing of $K(i)\wedge\Phi^H(-)$.

Every occurring finite group is a $p$-group. The class of occurring groups is closed under subgroups and quotients. If $A$ is any section of an occurring group, its minimum number of generators satisfies $d(A)\le l$.

Let $f:Y\to Z$ be a finite covering of finite groupoids. Choose a common stage $L$ as in [thm:pro-characters](#thm:pro-characters), and a label $\alpha:BL\to Z$. If the pullback of $f$ is the finite $L$-set $S$, then the evaluation of $f_!(1)\in\pi_0 A_Z$ at $\alpha$ is $|S^L|\,1_{D_L}$.

Let $F$ be finite, let $z\in\pi_0A_F$, and suppose that an evaluation at an advanced stage satisfies $\chi_\alpha(z)=r\cdot1_D$ for $r\in\mathbb Q$. Then $r\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}$. If the restriction of $z$ to the underlying point of $BF$ is zero in $\pi_0\mathbf 1$, then $r\in p\mathbb Z_{(p)}$.

For every finite group $F$, $$\label{eq:hom-integrality}
 \frac{|\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma,F)|}{|F|}\in\mathbb Z_{(p)}.$$

Let $E$ be a pro-$p$ group.*

1.  *Every finite section of $E$ is a section of a finite quotient of $E$. If all finite sections of $E$ have generator number at most $l$, then every closed subgroup of $E$ is topologically generated by at most $l$ elements.*

2.  *A procyclic pro-$p$ group is either trivial, finite cyclic, or isomorphic to $\mathbb Z_p$. Every continuous epimorphism $K\twoheadrightarrow
    \mathbb Z_p$ splits.*

3.  *A finitely generated pro-$p$ group with infinite abelianization has a continuous epimorphism onto $\mathbb Z_p$.

Let $K$ be a pro-$p$ group and let $d,l\geq0$. Suppose $K\times\mathbb Z_p^d$ satisfies the subgroup congruences and all its finite sections have generator number at most $l$. If $K\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z_p$ has kernel $N$, then $N\times\mathbb Z_p^{d+1}$ has both properties.

For $d\geq1$, let $a_j(d)$ be the number of open subgroups of index $p^j$ in $\mathbb Z_p^d$. Then $$\label{eq:lattice-generating-function}
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{j\geq0}a_j(d)t^j
       &=\prod_{u=0}^{d-1}(1-p^u t)^{-1},\\
 \lim_{j\to\infty}a_j(d)
       &=c_d:=\prod_{u=1}^{d-1}(1-p^u)^{-1}\ne0
 \quad\text{in }\mathbb Z_p.
 \end{aligned}$$
Let $K$ be a nontrivial finitely generated pro-$p$ group and $d\geq1$. If $K\times\mathbb Z_p^d$ satisfies the subgroup congruences, then $K$ has infinite abelianization.

For every finite $p$-group $P$ and every $l\geq0$, $$\bigl(U_P(L_{T(l)}S)\bigr)_{\mathbb Q}\ne0
       \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell(P,1)\leq l.$$

Let $P$ be a finite $p$-group, and let $k,l\geq0$. If $$\ell\bigl(P\times(C_{p^r})^k,1\bigr)\leq l
          \qquad\text{for every }r\geq1,$$ then $k+\ell(P,1)\leq l$.
Let $R$ be a unital associative ring spectrum and $k\ge0$. Then $$T(k)\wedge R\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad K(k)\wedge R\ne0.$$
If $k>0$ and $B$ is a nonzero commutative algebra in $\mathrm{Sp}_{K(k)}$, then its unit has nonzero image in $\pi_0B\otimes\mathbb Q$.
Let $B$ be a nonzero commutative $E$-algebra in $\mathrm{Sp}_{K(k)}$. For every $r\ge1$, put $C=(C_{p^r})^k$. Then $$\bigl(U_C(B)\bigr)_{\mathbb Q}\ne0.$$

For finite groups $P,C$ and an ordinary commutative ring spectrum $D$, there is a natural unit-preserving map $$U_{P\times C}(D)\longrightarrow U_C(U_P(D)),$$ where each displayed cofree construction uses the trivial action on its coefficient algebra.

Let $z\in\mathcal C_m^G$ be the image of a finite genuine $G$-spectrum, and let $n\le m$. Suppose that $B\le G$ satisfies $$m-n<\ell(G,B),$$ and that every $(K,k)\in\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(z)$ with $k<m$ satisfies $$\ell(G,K)\le k-n.$$ Then $z$ and $B$ satisfy both orthogonality conditions in [lem:layer-splitting](#lem:layer-splitting).

Let $G$ be any finite group, $p$ a prime, $H,K\le G$, and $m,n\ge0$. Then $$\mathcal P_m^G(K)\subseteq\mathcal P_n^G(H)$$ if and only if there is a conjugate $K^g=gKg^{-1}\le H$ such that $$N=O^p(H)=O^p(K^g),\qquad
 m\ge n+\ell(H/N,K^g/N).$$ In particular, the numerical test is applied to a qualifying conjugate in the finite $p$-group $H/N$.
